Script:


Cabinet Bloodbath final Script SECTION ONE AND PROMO’S FINAL

Commentary One
On Monday this week, the rand was trading at a two year high, and Finance Minister Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas were on an international investment roadshow. Yesterday he sat down with me at Treasury

Bongani
So as you got on that plane last week, everything was all systems go?

Pravin Gordhan
Absolutely. Remember that the group that we were going to meet on Monday and Tuesday control 5 trillion dollars of money. `They can choose to bring it to SA or take it to Indonesia to …our job to convince them to bring the money to South Africa

Link
And then came the order for the minister and his deputy to return home immediately. It came directly from the top

Pravin
It was an SMS when I landed at Heathrow at 6 am in the morning
Bongani
From the president
Pravin
From the presidency
Bongani
When you received that sms did you want to rub your eyes
Pravin Gordhan
Well it was surprising that it came

Commentary Two
But says former top six ANC stalwart Cheryl Carolus, the sms was designed to inflict maximum humiliation

Cheryl Carolus
The calculated cruelty with which the president behaves towards two comrades. Just remember he had given them permission to go. He wanted to humiliate them and that is so inhumane so disloyal so despicable. He lets them fly out and it is as if he wants to inflict max pain and embarrassment.

Commentary Three
Fifteen months ago, Pravin Gordhan took the job as finance minister for the second time after Nenegate wiped billions out of the economy. He is widely regarded as the man who has kept treasury safe from the rent seekers. For his troubles he has been harassed, and falsely charged with trumped up charges that were later withdrawn


Bongani
How bad did the pressure get
Pravin
Well I don’t think it is very nice to besmirched have your family threatened… misinformation and fake news… risk of a charge – investigation – appearances in court …we had the best lawyers in South Africa saying there is no substance here

Commentary Four
On Tuesday this week, the ministers legal team was in court, opposing the Gupta family, who wanted the minister to force the banks to reopen their accounts. President Jacob Zuma also attempted to enter the legal dispute between the minister and the Gupta-controlled companies but his legal team then made a hasty departure from the courtroom after Gauteng Judge President Dunstan Mlambo castigated him for taking three months to react.

Pravin
You have heard all the goings on in the courts and We await the courts decision

Commentary five
As the case got underway, Gordhan landed. Later he was seen at Luthuli house, prompting speculation that he would get axed

Pravin
We were still trying to figure out why we were called back. We had contact with the SG and he said come over it had nothing to do with the sms I had received

Bongani
So what were you eventually told was the reason for your recall?
Pravin
Oh no we were not given any reason
Bongani
To this moment
Yes
You do understand the surprise on my face
Pravin
Yes of course

Commentary six
As speculation grew, that the President would soon fire one of his best performing ministers, South Africans also woke to the news that giant of the ANC liberation movement, Ahmed Kathrada had died.

Inevitably, On Wednesday the political temperature rose, at Kathrada’s funeral attended by the finance minister. But the President decided that he would not attend in line with the family’s wishes



Up sound

Former president Kgalema Mothlanthe read Kathrada’s plea for President Zuma to step down.

Kathrada
Is it asking too much to express the hope …to consider stepping down
Crowd cheers

Commentary Seven
By Wednesday it was already a big week, with stories swishing across our political landscape. But the story that grabbed attention was this amateur report, accusing the Finance minister of wanting to overthrow the government.

Bongani
When the intelligence report What was your reaction

PRAVIN
Anger on the one hand and you just shake your head and say how stupid can you get. We are democrats. On the one hand, we are doing everything we are doing to protect South Africa and advance its interests. Why should we be the so- called saboteurs?

Commentary Eight
Chairperson of Corruption watch Mavuso Msimang also belongs to ANC veterans group 101

Mavuso
To be told that the reason is that he was involved in some kind of conspiracy – that is really hogwash with due respect to whoever compiled it and that really upset me

Commentary nine
On Thursday morning the communist party confirmed the president wanted to fire his minister and use the discredited report as leverage. They had objected.

Up sound Solly
Suffice to say this intelligence report is part of the reason given why this Comrade was brought back and we still objected to that

Commentary ten
But there was more to come after the SACP revelations. The EFF issued papers in the Constitutional Court.  They want the court to compel the Speaker of Parliament to institute disciplinary proceedings against President Jacob Zuma as a precursor to his impeachment, and the DA leader said he would bring a motion of no confidence against the president

LINK
After days of speculation the country was on tenterhooks. Would he or wouldn’t he, and then the news broke. Gupta owned television ANN 7 declared to the country the president had fired 15 ministers and deputy ministers



Commentary eleven
Around midnight it soon became clear that Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas were out.

Up sound President
I have decided to make changes to the national executive in order to improve efficiency and effectiveness

Bongani
And then of course in the midst of this, anxiety grew around the country as we all thought its coming and then indeed the axe fell
Pravin
you can train yourself not to lose sleep over some of those things one learns to live with that – nothing is guaranteed for life and then learn to move on

Bongani
How were you told
PRAVIN
I wasn’t told I learnt through a TV screen
Bongani
That is extraordinary
Pravin
That is life

Commentary twelve
The new finance minister is Malusi Gigaba and his deputy is Sifiso Buthelezi. In total 5 ministers and two deputies were axed. Tina Joemat Pieterson, Dipuo Peters, Derek Hanekom and Ngoako Ramatlodi lost their jobs.

Bongani
Is this our lowest moment since 1994?
Cheryl Carolus
I would say yes, JZ has decided to wrench away the real control of who runs this country to himself and a group of greedy mercenary people he has decided to take the running of this country away from the ANC

Commentary thirteen
Many believe that the Gupta family are now firmly in charge and the president would use more pliable ministers as puppets to loot the treasury. Newly formed South African Federated union head Zwelenzima Vavi agrees.

VAVI
How dare do you use the legitimacy of the organization to hand over this country to a small family that doesn’t have a single scratch to show in any fight against the apartheid system

ADD BREAK HERE Duration: 9 min 43

SECTION TWO CABINET RESHUFFLE FINAL SCRIPT

LINK
Reaction has been a chorus of condemnation – opposition parties, civil society business labour and even three ANC officials broke ranks with the president saying they had not been consulted

Commentary Fourteen
Secretary General Gwede Mantashe squirmed when pressed about the decision on 702

Up Sound
My own view as the Secretary General, is that I felt like the list was developed somewhere else.

Mavuso
You know Gwede Mantashe, I really pitied him this morning when he said …you know they came to tell us we have really been informed and not consulted …well they have built this cult around the individual called Jacob Zuma

Xolani Gwala
But he must know that the ANC is unhappy with these changes.
Gwede
He must not know he knows

Mavuso
He says he doesn’t know where this was discussed and this is what we are expected to live with and expect that the people will endorse it come 2019 they had better think hard

Commentary fifteen
Deputy president Cyril Ramaphosa, finally spoke out against the president

Cyril Ramaphosa
I raised my concern and objection on the removal of the minister of finance

Mavuso
The deputy president must understand that the omelet of being a president, in order to eat that, he has got to break the egg

Commentary sixteen
On Friday, angry South Africans gathered outside treasury

Up sound

Inside Pravin Gordhan and his deputy Mcebisi Jonas addressed a press conference

Pravin
One thing we must emphasis is that our souls are not for sale and we hope that more and more SA clear that our country is not for sale

Up sound applause

MCEBISI JONAS
You don’t have to be a genius to see the trend in the country. You have in front of you history that is unfolding and democracy that is being undermined and some of those are diversions of state resources to serve limited interests.

UP SOUND Senzeni na

VOX POP 1
I have a one year old child. Please leave so that child can have a good future
VOX POP2
This is selling our country to the Gupta’s come on

Cheryl Carolus
Parliament had censured minister Bathabile Dlamini, Faith Muthambi. These two comrades of ours have been derelect they have been reckless, and may have acted unlawfully and what does the president do? The president promotes and rewards them, so the president is cocking a snook at the members of parliament elected by the public. And then he punishes the people that parliament actually has felt has done a good job like the leaders of the treasury minister Gordhan and Jonas. So I think the president has rubbished the ANC and and has rubbished parliament. I don’t care what you think it doesn’t matter

Commentary seventeen
On Friday morning, the banks lost R83 billion rand of their market cap. Investment solutions Chief economist Lesiba Mothata

Lesiba Mothata
There is a lot of concern. Bank shares have already been declining and upon the news when Johannesburg opened at the JSE we have seen about a– about 5% decline in bank shares and that is ominous

Commentary eighteen
But he says its still too early to panic

Bongani
So are you saying this is not a meltdown?
Lesiba
We are not there yet – crisis will look like this: When you have immediate downgrade, there will be a need for an immediate IMF bailout, a systemic banking failure, a central bank that is beginning to hike interest rates seen it in Brazil and Russia.

Commentary nineteen
Lesiba says treasury as an institution is bigger than any single individual

Lesiba Mothata
The national treasury is of world class standards. The new ones that are coming in could pick up and make it better – or they will have to exert huge amount of effort to destroy such deep caliber of institution

Commentary twenty
Kathrada’s widow Barbara Hogan has called for the removal of the president, describing his actions as dastardly deeds done in dark corners

Mavuso
This week has been a week of shame. People also ask me sometimes what would Tambo who I worked with have done – hypothetical to be sure I know that like AK he would probably find himself asking the president to go. We are not used to people at the helm of leadership get accused of rape, being bribed. But difficult times require hard decisions and we have been afraid to make the hard decisions.

Commentary twenty- one
Even ANC alliance partner, the SACP has called for Jacob Zuma to step down. But he is on record saying he is not going anywhere

Cheryl
I refuse to accept that I am powerless, I still believe that as we have indeed seen most men and women in the ANC are very decent people. What the president has done is that they have arrogated to themselves more and more power and acted without the democratic
Bongani
So what do they do?
Cheryl
I am not about to go and join another party – I want my ANC back
Bongani
How are you going to get it back
Cheryl
Well the quiet work we have done up to now, we are going to have to change tack
Bongani
Surely you have to say enough is enough
Cheryl
Bongani I agree with you and I am on the record for saying the president must step down.
These actions of this shuffle he has not only ignored the ANC but he has trashed the ANC and its democratic structures
Bongani
What are you as the ANC going to do about it
Cheryl
I am putting a challenge to every ANC member and cabinet. They are going to have to use their power of the ANC might. I think we have to cross that line ourselves. we cannot behave like we have. The president has crossed the line. That is unforgivable
Commentary twenty- Two
On Friday ratings agency Fitch warned that it could review its outlook on South Africa, following the cabinet reshuffle. Even now P Gordhan says we cannot risk a downgrade.

Gordhan
we must aim to avoid a downgrade, that was what we were trying to do in London and I hope we have succeeded
Bongani
What next for you?
Gordhan
I want to take a break still an MP, start thinking about the next chapter continue with activism in some form or another

Commentary Twenty- Three
Stepping into his huge shoes is Minister Malusi Gigaba. He will be South Africa’s fourth finance minister in 15 months

Malusi Gigaba
For too long ……this is a people’s government

Commentary Twenty- four
He told a press conference that he “needed space” and committed Treasury to sound financial policies to keep the national debt under control. Meanwhile the political storm is gathering momentum as the opposition calls for the Presidents head.

Bongani
You were an activist, you went to exile do you still have the stamina for a political fight
Mavuso
To the last day of my living I will not sit idle and fold my hands when things like this happen. This situation requires all of us who have an interest in the country to come forward and do something about it.

Commentary Twenty- Five
Meanwhile the former finance minister is keeping his cards close to his chest.

Bongani
You have talked about connecting the dots and doing the right thing what do you mean
Pravin
No I will spell it out when the time is right. I want to retire peacefully now.

THE END: 9 50







PROMO ONE
We speak to Former Finance minister Pravin Gordhan

Bongani
How were you told
PRAVIN
I wasn’t told I learnt through a TV screen
Bongani
That is extraordinary

PROMO TWO
There has been widespread outrage to President Zuma’s cabinet reshuffle

Cheryl Carolus
These actions of this shuffle he has not only ignored the ANC but he has trashed the ANC and its democratic decision making structures

Even now P Gordhan says we cannot risk a downgrade. Gordhan we must aim to avoid a downgrade, that was what we were trying to do in London and I hope we have succeeded Bongani What next for you? Gordhan I want to take a break still an MP, start thinking about the next chapter continue with activism in some form or another Commentary Twenty- Three Stepping into his huge shoes is Minister Malusi Gigaba. He will be South Africa’s fourth finance minister in 15 months Malusi Gigaba For too long ……this is a people’s government Commentary Twenty- four He told a press conference that he “needed space” and committed Treasury to sound financial policies to keep the national debt under control. Meanwhile the political storm is gathering momentum as the opposition calls for the Presidents head. Bongani You were an activist, you went to exile do you still have the stamina for a political fight Mavuso To the last day of my living I will not sit idle and fold my hands when things like this happen. This situation requires all of us who have an interest in the country to come forward and do something about it. Commentary Twenty- Five Meanwhile the former finance minister is keeping his cards close to his chest. Bongani You have talked about connecting the dots and doing the right thing what do you mean Pravin No I will spell it out when the time is right. I want to retire peacefully now.
